The volume of a cube-shaped container is increasing. Find the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the container is changing with respect to the side length at the moment when the face diagonal of the cube is equal to $10\sqrt{2}\,\text{cm}.$

The instantaneous rate of change at the moment when the face diagonal is $10\sqrt{2}$ centimeters is equal to
{{field-1}} ${\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{cm}.$
worked_solution:
Since we are given that the face diagonal of the cube is $10\sqrt{2}\,\text{cm}$, its side length $s$ is $10\,\text{cm}.$ Now, the volume of a cube with side length $s$ is given by 

$$
V=V(s)={s}^{3}.
$$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $V(s)$ with respect to $s$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}({s}^{3}) \\  & =3{s}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $s=10$ gives

$$
{V}^{′}(10)=3(10)^{2}=300.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the container is increasing when the face diagonal is $10\sqrt{2}\,\text{cm}$ is $300\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{cm}.$
